chunks: At the center is the processor, an SoC in a phone with CPU, GPU, neural engine, image signal processor and memory controllers; in a laptop it can be an SoC too, or a CPU plus a separate GPU and chipset.
Next to it is DRAM and flash storage: LPDDR and UFS in a phone, DDR or LPDDR and an NVMe SSD in a laptop.

Power is its own subsystem: a lithium-ion battery with a fuel gauge and protection, a charger IC that handles USB-C power negotiation, and a PMIC or a set of buck converters and LDOs that make the many rails the chips need, with sequencing.
Then connectivity: cellular modem in a phone, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth in both, GNSS, NFC, each with antennas and RF front-end modules.
On the human side: display with a driver and touch controller, backlight or OLED power, speakers, microphones and audio codec, cameras with MIPI links, keyboard and trackpad in a laptop.
Plus sensors: IMU, light and proximity, magnetometer, temperature sensors. Holding it together are the board, shielding, thermal path, and a lot of firmware.
The constraints I'd call out are battery life, heat, size and cost, and that radios and high-speed digital have to coexist without interfering with each other."
